answer.answer: A draft register entry for admissions-portal processing of undergraduate applicants' data; a person checks each field, adds what is missing, and saves it.

draft.name: Undergraduate admissions applications

draft.dataCategories: Names; contact details; Class XII marks; category certificates
draft.collectionSource: From applicants, through the admissions portal

law.point: Some undergraduate applicants fresh from Class XII may be under eighteen. Before processing a child's data, the university must obtain verifiable consent from a parent or lawful guardian.
A child is anyone who has not completed eighteen years of age, so applicants' ages matter here.
Sets how to check that the person giving consent for a child is an identifiable adult parent. It applies from 13 May 2027.
Processing needs a lawful ground: either consent or one of the 'certain legitimate uses' in s.7. The description does not say which, so counsel to confirm.
Where consent is relied on, applicants must first get a notice (an information statement) listing the data, the purpose and how to exercise their rights.
Marks and certificates are used to make an admission decision, so the university must keep them complete, accurate and consistent.
Data must be erased once the purpose is served, for example after admissions close, unless another law requires it to be kept.
Personal data and processing logs must be kept for at least one year from processing, then erased unless another law requires longer.

missingInformation: Whether any applicants are under eighteen, and how parental consent is obtained if so
Which lawful ground is relied on (consent or a legitimate use), for counsel to confirm
How long application data is kept for unsuccessful and successful applicants
Who the data is shared with (for example vendors running the portal, affiliated colleges or regulators)
Security safeguards on the admissions portal (access control, encryption, logs, backups)
Whether the portal is hosted or the data is processed outside India
Whether any automated or AI tool helps shortlist or rank applicants
The owning department (likely Admissions) and the notice shown to applicants

answer.answer: This is a draft reply to an access request under s.11, for a person and counsel to complete and check before sending.

draft.letter:
Dear [Name],

Our reference: [reference]
[date]

Your request for information about your personal data

Thank you for your email, which we received on 20 October 2026. We have recorded it as a request for access to information about your personal data.

What you asked for
You asked for a summary of the personal data that Mumbai University holds about you, and for details of who that personal data has been shared with.

The right you are using
Section 11(1) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 gives a Data Principal (the person the data is about) the right to ask an organisation for:
- a summary of the personal data it is processing about them, and of the processing activities it carries out with that data;
- the identities of the other organisations it has shared the data with, meaning other Data Fiduciaries (organisations that decide how personal data is used) and Data Processors (service providers that process data on its behalf), with a description of the data shared; and
- any other information about the data and its processing that the law prescribes.

The Act sets out a limited exception for certain sharing with bodies authorised by law, made on a written request for the prevention, detection or investigation of offences or cyber incidents (section 11(2)). [Whether any part of this exception applies — to be decided by the person handling this request, with counsel.]

We have already confirmed your identity, so we do not need any further details from you to deal with this request.

Our response
[What we did and what we are providing — to be completed by the person handling this request.]

[Summary of the personal data we process about you and our processing activities — to be completed by the person handling this request.]

[The organisations with which your personal data has been shared, and a description of the data shared with each — to be completed by the person handling this request.]

[Any part of the request we are not able to meet, and the reason — to be completed by the person handling this request, with counsel.]

Timing
We will respond fully no later than 18 January 2027. [Date of this response, if sent earlier — to be completed.]

Questions and concerns
If you have questions about how we process your personal data, please contact: [name or role, email address and telephone number of the person who can answer on behalf of Mumbai University].

If you are not satisfied with our response, you can raise a grievance with us using [our grievance redressal process — link or details to be added]. If your grievance is not resolved, you may then make a complaint to the Data Protection Board of India, the body set up under the Act. The Act asks that you use our grievance process first.

Yours sincerely,

[Name]
[Role]
Mumbai University
draft.summary: Access to information request under s.11, received by email on 20 October 2026; identity recorded as verified; respond-by date 18 January 2027 (the ninety-day ceiling). The Data Principal asked for a summary of the personal data the university holds about them and the organisations it has been shared with. The draft response explains the s.11(1) right, notes the s.11(2) exception for consideration, and gives contact and grievance routes. Outcome: [what was provided, partly provided or not provided — to be completed by the person handling this request]. Exception under s.11(2) considered: [yes/no and reason — counsel to confirm]. Date sent: [date]. Sent by: [name/role]. A person closes this request in the register; the assistant does not.

law.point: A Data Principal can ask for a summary of their personal data and its processing, and the identities of other Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors it was shared with, with a description of the data shared.

The details of sharing need not be given where data was shared with a body authorised by law, on its written request, to prevent, detect or investigate offences or cyber incidents. Whether this applies is a judgement for a person and counsel.
Grievances must be answered within a reasonable period not exceeding ninety days; the respond-by date of 18 January 2027 reflects that ceiling.
Every response to a rights request must give the business contact details of a person who can answer questions about the processing.
The Data Principal has a right to readily available grievance redressal, so the letter points to the university's grievance route.
The Data Principal must use the organisation's grievance process before approaching the Board.
A request is made using the means and particulars the Data Fiduciary requires; as identity is recorded as verified, no further particulars are requested.
Rules 9 and 14 come into force on 13 May 2027, after this request was received; counsel to confirm how they apply to it.

What personal data the university processes about this person and its processing activities, from the relevant systems and registers.
The organisations (other Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors) the data was shared with, and what was shared with each.
Whether the s.11(2) exception applies to any sharing — counsel to confirm.
The name or role and contact details of the person who can answer questions on the university's behalf.
Details of the university's grievance redressal process to quote in the letter.
Counsel to confirm whether s.11 is in force for this request, as the Act's commencement notification is not in the corpus and Rules 9 and 14 apply from 13 May 2027.

law.point: The university must erase the personal data when asked, unless keeping it is necessary for the specified purpose or to comply with a law.
The university must erase data once its purpose is no longer served, and make its Data Processors (vendors) erase data it gave them, unless a law requires it to be kept.
The right to erasure covers data the person gave with consent, including data volunteered for a specified purpose under s.7(a).
Every response to a rights request must give the business contact details of someone who can answer questions about the processing. This Rule applies from 13 May 2027.
Grievances must be answered within a published period not exceeding ninety days. This Rule applies from 13 May 2027.
From 13 May 2027, personal data, traffic data and processing logs must be kept for at least one year from the processing. This may affect what can be erased now.
The person must use the university's grievance process before complaining to the Board.
